Porte-Saint-Denis (10e arr.) — Paris, France

🟡 Local press research

Average day Average night

In detail

This quartier covers Boulevard de Strasbourg and rue du Château-d'Eau, where a prefectural order (issued December 2024, extended through May 2026) forces many shops — largely Afro-Caribbean hair salons — to close between 8pm and 5am, and bans off-premises alcohol sales overnight, citing 'repeated disturbances to public order,' unauthorised street occupation and unlicensed vending. The measure is genuinely controversial (Paris Council rejected a motion against it in October 2025, with critics saying it stigmatises the businesses rather than fixing the underlying disorder), but its existence confirms real, official-level nighttime nuisance concerns in this exact strip. Daytime is mostly just crowded and commercial. Sources checked: Mairie du 10e, 'Arrêté préfectoral: les commerces fermés dès 20h à Château d'Eau', Dec 2024; Groupe Écologiste de Paris, council motion on the closure order, Oct 2025.
